items.title: Burnham defends Jackdaw decision as Badenoch urges PM to overturn ban on new oil and gas licences
items.summary: The UK government says the field, which is opposed by environmental campaigners, could be producing gas by the end of this month.

items.title: Websites taken down worldwide as critical cyber-security update issued
items.summary: The vulnerabilities with PHP, a programming language widely used across the internet, have been described as the most significant ever found by AI.

items.title: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: Moscow says it is "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and US President Donald Trump says the world is "the closest we've been" to ending the war.

items.title: Rosenberg: US diplomatic push offers little hope for imminent Ukraine peace
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin does not feel under pressure right now to end the war, the BBC's Russia Editor writes.

items.title: Criminals who skip sentencing will face solitary confinement or lose social visits
items.summary: Judges will be given new powers to impose tougher prison punishments on offenders who refuse to face their victims' families during sentencing.

items.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
items.summary: Drugs will be tested simultaneously, which it's hoped will speed up the process of finding new treatments for this common type of dementia.

items.title: UK's gaps in Arctic defence leave it open to Russian attacks, committee warns
items.summary: A report by MPs urges the UK to address capability gaps including a lack of Royal Navy warships and submarines, as Russia seeks to dominate the region.

items.title: The 'trillion pound' oil fund the government believes Britain could have built
items.summary: For the first time, the Treasury calculates how much the UK could have raised by investing North Sea proceeds.
